hiya, can you help me write a firm but polite email to my old letting agent? they want to keep £640 of our £1,150 deposit for "professional cleaning" (£280) and a "damaged" bedroom carpet (£360). the carpet was ALREADY worn when we moved in, it's literally in the check-in inventory (page 7, photo 23). we left the place spotless, I have 41 photos timestamped 31/08.

tenancy ended 31 August 2026. deposit is protected with the DPS, they said I can raise a dispute but I'd rather sort it with the agent first.

details:
me - ⟦name|Siobhán Mac Giolla Phádraig⟧ (everyone calls me ⟦name|Shiv⟧ so don't panic about the spelling lol)
old flat - ⟦street address|Flat 3, 27 Ravenswood Terrace, Leeds LS6 2QH⟧
new address for post -
⟦street address|14 Cardigan Lane
Headingley
Leeds
LS6 3BJ⟧
agent = Harbour & Finch Lettings, the guy dealing with it is ⟦name|Tom Ellery-Hughes⟧, ⟦email address|t.ellery-hughes@harbourandfinch.co.uk⟧
landlord is a Mr ⟦name|R. Okonjo⟧, never met him
tenancy ref on their emails is HF/LDS/2291
my mobile is ⟦phone number|07700 900314⟧ if they'd rather ring

also - I watched a Martin Lewis thing that said it's on THEM to prove the damage is beyond fair wear and tear, is that right?? and my flatmate ⟦name|Priyanka⟧ was on the tenancy too, should it come from both of us?

Assistant
Broadly, yes. With a protected deposit the agent has to justify any deduction. If it goes to the DPS's free dispute service, the adjudicator starts from the position that the deposit belongs to the tenants, and the agent needs evidence (check-in and check-out reports, photos, invoices) showing damage beyond fair wear and tear. A carpet already recorded as worn at check-in is a strong point in your favour, and cleaning charges usually only stand if the property was handed back less clean than it was let.

Since ⟦name|Priyanka⟧ was a joint tenant, it's best to send it from both of you, or at least copy her in so the agent can't say they only heard from one of you.

Here's a draft you can adapt:

Subject: Deposit deductions – ⟦street address|Flat 3, 27 Ravenswood Terrace, LS6 2QH⟧ (your ref HF/LDS/2291)

Dear ⟦name|Tom⟧,

Thank you for your email of 9 October setting out the proposed deductions from our deposit. We don't agree to them, for the reasons below.

1. Carpet (£360). The check-in inventory dated 1 September 2024 records the bedroom carpet as "worn, light staining by window" (page 7, photo 23). Its condition at check-out reflects that plus two years of normal use, which is fair wear and tear.

2. Professional cleaning (£280). We cleaned the flat thoroughly before returning the keys and have 41 dated photographs taken on 31 August 2026. Please send us the check-out report and any invoice you are relying on for this charge.

We'd ask you to return the full deposit of £1,150 within 14 days of this email. If we can't resolve this between us, we will raise a dispute with the DPS and submit the inventory and photographs as evidence.

Kind regards,

⟦name|Siobhán Mac Giolla Phádraig⟧ and ⟦name|Priyanka⟧ [surname]
Forwarding address: ⟦street address|14 Cardigan Lane, Headingley, Leeds LS6 3BJ⟧
Mobile: ⟦phone number|07700 900314⟧

A few tips:
• Attach page 7 of the inventory and a handful of the clearest photos rather than all 41.
• Keep it in writing so there's a paper trail if you do go to the DPS.
• Check the dates: the agent should have protected the deposit within 30 days of you paying it and sent you the prescribed information. If they didn't, that changes things considerably.

amazing thank you!! ⟦name|Pri⟧ says her surname is ⟦name|Raghunathan⟧ 😅 also one more thing, they still have a scan of my passport from the right to rent check, number ⟦passport number|563019284⟧, can I make them delete it now we've left?

Assistant
Good thinking. You can ask, but don't expect it to be deleted straight away: landlords and agents are required to keep copies of Right to Rent documents for the length of the tenancy and for one year after it ends, so they're entitled to hold it until roughly the end of August 2027. What you can reasonably ask for is confirmation of how long they'll keep it and that it will be securely destroyed after that.

You could add this paragraph before the sign-off:

"Separately, please confirm how long you will retain the copy of ⟦name|Siobhán⟧'s passport taken for the Right to Rent check, and that it will be securely deleted at the end of the statutory retention period."

And change the sign-off to: ⟦name|Siobhán Mac Giolla Phádraig⟧ and ⟦name|Priyanka Raghunathan⟧.

One small thing: you don't need to include the passport number in the email itself. They already have it, and the fewer places it's written down, the better.

Send the dispute in writing, certified mail with return receipt, well before 11/13. Keep copies of everything. Do NOT agree on the phone that the debt is yours or "make a small payment to show good faith." Paid medical collections aren't supposed to show on your reports at all, so if this is on there, dispute it with all three bureaus too.

Chapter 3: In Which Mr. Collins Brings a Petition

The bell over the door of Longbourn Books had two notes, and Elizabeth Bennet had learned to read them like weather. A bright double chime meant a browser. A long, sour clang meant someone had pushed the door with their shoulder because their hands were full of clipboards.

It was the clang.

"Cousin Elizabeth," said Mr. Collins, beaming as though he had been invited. "I come bearing democracy."

"You come bearing a clipboard."

"A petition," he corrected, and laid it on the counter between a stack of water-damaged Trollopes and the jar of free bookmarks. "To the new owner of the building. Lady Catherine feels, and I agree, that the façade should be restored to its 1890s colour scheme."

"Lady Catherine doesn't live on this street."

"Lady Catherine," said Mr. Collins, "lives on every street, in a sense."

Charlotte Lucas, who was supposed to be shelving Poetry and was instead eating a sausage roll behind the Poetry shelf, made a noise like a kettle.

The double chime. Elizabeth looked up, and there he was: Fitzwilliam Darcy, in a coat that cost more than her stock, holding a paper cup and the expression of a man who has just been told that the coffee next door is "small-batch."

"Mr. Darcy," said Mr. Collins, and bowed. Actually bowed. From the waist.

Darcy looked at the clipboard, then at Elizabeth, then, briefly and unforgivably, at the hand-lettered sign above the till: STAFF PICK: MANSFIELD PARK (IT'S BETTER THAN YOU THINK).

"It isn't," he said.

"I beg your pardon?"

"Better than I think. I think quite highly of it already. Your sign assumes I don't."

Charlotte choked on her sausage roll.

"Mr. Collins," Elizabeth said, very sweetly, "Mr. Darcy owns the building now. Perhaps you'd like to show him your petition. I'm sure he's dying to repaint the front. In mauve."

"Heliotrope," said Mr. Collins reverently.

Darcy took the clipboard. He read every line. He took a pen from his inside pocket (a fountain pen, of course it was a fountain pen), wrote something at the bottom, and handed it back. Mr. Collins read it, and his face did something complicated, and he left without bowing.

When the clang had faded, Elizabeth held out her hand. Darcy, after a moment, put the clipboard in it.

Under the forty-one signatures, thirty-eight of them Mr. Collins's in different pens, he had written: The façade will remain as it is. Rent on Unit 2 is frozen until further notice. — F.D.

She looked up. He was already at the door.

"Why?" she said.

The double chime. "Because," said Mr. Darcy, without turning round, "your sign was right about Mansfield Park."

#2
0x800f0922 at that stage is very often the EFI System Partition being too full for the new boot files. Open an admin Command Prompt and run:

[CODE]
mountvol Y: /s
dir /s Y:\EFI
[/CODE]

If it's a 100 MB ESP with only a few MB free, look for vendor junk under Y:\EFI (old BIOS recovery files, font folders from ancient updaters). Don't touch \EFI\Microsoft\Boot. Copy anything you delete to a USB stick first.

Also, friendly reminder that this forum is public and indexed by Google. You might want to take your email out of your signature, ⟦name|Gareth⟧.

⟦username|grumpy_gareth_w⟧ · Thread starter · 17 Oct 2026
#3
Bang on. 100 MB partition, 3.8 MB free. There was a folder Y:\EFI\Dell\Bios\Recovery with 61 MB of .rcv files from 2022. Copied them to a stick, deleted, ran the update: installed first go, now on 26100.2161.
